objective: Coding-agent lint rules and codebase inertia
scope: Python 3.12, ML/data processing, PostgreSQL/SQL, Terraform/AWS, containers, shell, CI and testing. Compare present scaffold controls and transferable cross-language design rules. Research only; do not implement or loosen gates.
outputFormat: Auditable Markdown report with prioritized candidate-rule matrix, concrete examples, source evidence, overlap, false positives, verification cost, and adoption recommendations.
decisionContext: Choose the next rules that prevent immediate defects and long-term codebase inertia before ML implementation in podium-forecastin-ml. User confirmed the six-question brief including inertia expansion.

questions.text: Which coding-agent behaviours introduce immediate defects or long-term codebase inertia, what evidence supports these effects, and which behaviours can be detected deterministically?
Which established Python linting, typing and architecture rules address gaps in our current configuration?
Which rules address ML/data-pipeline correctness, particularly leakage, reproducibility, schema handling and external side effects?
Which additional SQL, Terraform, container, shell and CI rules fit our stack?
Which design constraints from other ecosystems would transfer usefully, and how could we enforce them?
Which candidates should we adopt first, defer or reject, considering evidence strength, overlap, false positives and maintenance cost?

constraints.targetAudience: Project owner and future implementing coding agents
constraints.existingKnowledge: Baseline commit 54b2c88: Ruff selected E F W I UP B N SIM C4 C90 PLR RUF T20 RET ARG PTH S; mypy strict; custom iteration depth, names, import layers, suppression/location/guidance guards; pytest; SQLFluff; Terraform/TFLint/Trivy; Docker Hadolint; ShellCheck; actionlint; Gitleaks. Baseline 103 tests plus single foundation seam.
constraints.notes: Confirmed by user in this task. Highly rated means adoption, active maintenance, practitioner experience and evidence of usefulness; popularity is not demonstrated coding-agent effectiveness. Acceptance: rule-level recommendations mapped to the current baseline; distinguish proven facts from proposed adaptations; validate sources, citations, hard constraints and rendered report completeness. Prefer dated primary material; versioned repository snapshots use their explicitly identified commit/release publication date, not retrieval dates. No implementation, live AWS changes or changes to verification gates.

allowed: Primary documentation, maintained repositories, original engineering accounts, academic research and transparent original industry analyses.
